brief: GS multi-topic What Matters Today note (Armbrust, FICC and Equities). It opens with today's calendar: the Trump-Xi meeting, Fed speakers Barkin, Hammack and Paulson, Jobless Claims, New Home Sales, and COST reporting post-close. META is down about 2% pre-market after its Connect keynote skewed toward hardware (the Muse gadget, VR goggles, audio-only smart glasses) over AI utility, disappointing some investors, though META also announced new retail partnerships for Muse. On agentic AI commerce, GS argues adoption will be gradual and category-dependent: it identifies $2.6tn of US consumer spending in high-likelihood categories and estimates roughly 2% agentic penetration of that spend could add about 1% to eCommerce growth; advertising monetization migrates with intent rather than disappearing; agentic payments build on existing infrastructure pending liability frameworks; and fraud/authorization risk may scale alongside legitimate adoption. Separately, 45% of S&P stocks now show negative beta to the index, an all-time high GS partly attributes to index concentration from AI capex and tech dominance, raising momentum-unwind risk; GS lists hedges (long index wings/correlation, RSP over SPX, momentum-index puts) if it reverts. GS's SMA survey finds record $255bn AUM (7.4% of hedge fund assets) at year-end 2025, with newer programs shifting toward capital-efficiency structures.
